Phoenician galleys dock at Tyre's stone breakwater. Dockworkers roll cedar logs toward Egyptian ships while purple-dye vats steam in workshops lining the quay.
Alexandria's Great Harbor swarms with grain vessels from Sicily. Lighthouse of Pharos towers above as stevedores haul amphoras up limestone steps toward warehouses.
Tang dynasty junks crowd Guangzhou's Pearl River docks. Persian merchants bargain over silk bales while porcelain crates swing from bamboo cranes onto waiting ships.
Lothal's brick-lined tidal dock fills at high tide. Indus merchants weigh carnelian beads on standardized scales beside ships loaded with Mesopotamian copper ingots.
Carthage's circular cothon harbor shelters war galleys. Merchants unload Spanish silver and Cornish tin onto quays where scribes tally cargo in Punic script.
Byblos harbor bustles as Egyptian timber ships receive cedar planks. Stone quays echo with Akkadian and hieroglyphic haggling over precious Lebanese wood shipments.
Srivijaya's Palembang wharves line the Musi River. Javanese outriggers unload cloves beside Indian dhows carrying cotton, while monks collect port taxes for Buddhist temples.
Adulis port on the Red Sea thrives with Aksumite trade. Incense and ivory pile high as Greek-speaking merchants negotiate with Arabian frankincense dealers.
Nile Delta shipyards hammer acacia planks into barges. Papyrus boat-builders work beside rope-makers twisting flax while grain ships await loading for Syrian ports.
Dilmun's Bahrain anchorage transfers Harappan carnelian to Sumerian merchants. Pearl-diving boats return as scribes record trade using both cuneiform and Indus seals.
Viking longships beach at Hedeby's wooden wharves. Frankish swords trade for Baltic amber and Slavic furs while Norse merchants repair clinker-built hulls.
Minoan Knossos harbor displays dolphin-painted warehouses. Wide stone basins shelter ships bearing octopus-ware pottery destined for Egyptian and Levantine markets.
Sidon's purple-dye workshops stain the harbor waters violet. Phoenician merchant ships load murex shells while Egyptian buyers inspect cloth bolts on crowded stone quays.
Ostia's Tiber mouth swarms with grain barges from Africa. Stevedores haul amphorae while harbor cranes swing marble blocks destined for Rome's endless construction.
Quanzhou's Song dynasty harbor bristles with masts from Arabia to Java. Porcelain, tea, and silk exchange hands as multilingual merchants crowd the bustling wharves.
Heian Japan's Naniwa port receives Korean ships bearing Buddhist sutras. Lacquerware and folding screens load onto vessels as imperial officials inspect tribute goods.
Tonle Sap's floating markets surround Khmer temple-ports. Wooden boats laden with rice, fish sauce, and ceramics navigate between stilt-house warehouses and trading posts.
Eridu's reed-boat harbor on the Persian Gulf handles Dilmun date shipments. Sumerian cuneiform tallies cargo as bitumen-caulked vessels unload copper from Magan.
Early Carthage trading post receives Iberian silver ships. Phoenician colonists unload cargo onto African shores while local Berber merchants offer grain and ivory.
Memphis shipyards construct royal barges for obelisk transport. Massive timber frames rise beside the Nile as workers waterproof hulls with pitch and linen.
Palembang's riverine warehouses store Maluku spices for redistribution. Srivijayan harbor masters coordinate between Cham, Chinese, and Indian merchant fleets anchored in tiers.
Piraeus basin shelters Athenian triremes between trading vessels. Amphorae of wine and olive oil await loading while Phoenician glass and Egyptian papyrus unload.
Birka's Lake Mälaren harbor trades Frankish glass beads for Arctic walrus ivory. Swedish merchants repair tar-sealed hulls while Slavic traders arrive with honey.
Goryeo celadon pottery loads onto Chinese merchant ships at Byeokrando. Korean harbor officials collect taxes as Song traders inspect jade-green glazed vessels.
Champa coastal temple-port receives Khmer tribute boats. Sandalwood and tortoiseshell pile beside brick sanctuaries as Malay sailors barter camphor for Indian cotton.
